plain.li: [theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:goat] Our goat has learned to open the gate. We have not yet learned to stop her. I will write again when one side wins.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The road between us is long, and I am told the potholes now have potholes.

[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:bridge] The bridge near us washed out again, and we are building it again, and it will wash out again. This is what passes for entertainment here.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:well] The well rope broke, and the bucket is still down there. We held a short service for it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I lost a boot in the mud on market day, and I am told it is still there, standing upright, like a monument to bad judgement.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:chickens] The chickens have moved into the shed and will not move out. We are negotiating, and losing.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Our cook has a new recipe. I am not allowed to say what is in it, and I would rather not know.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I counted the sheep three times this week and got three different answers, so either I cannot count or the sheep are up to something.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We repainted the gate and the rain came the very next morning, which I have decided to take personally.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Somebody keeps eating the last of the bread. I have my suspicions, and all of them have four legs.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] My handwriting gets worse every year and my eyes get worse to match, so perhaps they cancel out.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] If this letter arrives chewed at one corner, blame the courier's dog and not me.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:mule] I bought a mule at the market. The mule did not agree to the sale and is still making its case.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:crow] A crow has learned to say my name. It only says it when I am trying to sleep.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We held a contest for the best soup in town. Everyone won, which is to say nobody spoke to the judges afterwards.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Our oldest neighbour says the weather was better in her day. Her day, as far as anyone can tell, also rained.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The last letter I sent anywhere went the long way round, by three towns and a river. I hope this one is braver.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] I have been asked to keep this letter businesslike. This is the one sentence that isn't.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] Our clerk insists every letter needs a third paragraph. This is it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:wary] We are careful with strangers here. Even the dog checks your boots before she lets you in.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:trade] Our prices are fair, our scales are honest, and our coffee is terrible. Two out of three is good for a town.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:duty] I have three more letters to answer today and a meeting about a fence, so forgive the haste.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:proud] We have the best well in the region, the oldest wall and the loudest market. I mention it only in passing.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,!jk:singer] My neighbour has taken up singing. I mention it only so that someone outside {TOWN} knows what we are going through.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] We had a wedding last week, and the cake survived the dog, which nobody expected.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,!jk:pumpkin] I tried to grow a pumpkin this year. It is now the size of a fist and has a name, so we cannot eat it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,!jk:cat] A cat is sitting on the corner of this page as I write, so forgive the crooked lines. She has decided the letter is hers.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] Somebody here has started keeping bees. Somebody else has started keeping well away from the first somebody.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] The children found a frog they believe is enchanted. It is not enchanted. It is barely a frog.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I meant to write sooner, but every time I sat down something needed mending, feeding or rescuing from a ditch.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,!jk:goat] The goat sends her regards, by which I mean she ate the first draft of this letter.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I have taken up whittling. So far I have made a spoon, a smaller spoon, and a great many splinters.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] We had a dance at the turn of the season, and I am still finding out whose feet I stood on.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I gave the one carrying this a pie for the road. If the pie has not arrived with the letter, assume the worst.
[theirs,joke,a:friend,warmly] I read your last letter so often the folds have gone soft. Write another before this one falls apart.
[theirs,joke,a:friend,warmly,jk:goat] You are the only person I write to who writes back, so you must put up with all my news, including the goat.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,m:friend] I told someone here about you the other day, and they asked if you were real. I said very.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,m:friend] I have started keeping a list of things to tell you, so the letters do not forget anything. The list is long.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,m:friend] I have read your letters aloud so often that the dog now perks up at your name.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:friend] Things are much as they were when I last wrote, which is to say busy and well enough.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] The snow is up to the windowsills, so we are all very well acquainted with each other by now.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] It is so cold that the ink froze in the pot, and I warmed it on the stove, which is why this letter smells faintly of soup.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,season:winter] Somebody built a snowman by the gate, and the dogs have been barking at it for two days.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] It is so hot here that the dogs have stopped chasing anything, and so have I.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] The flies this summer are the size of small birds, and the small birds have given up.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:spring] Spring has come, and with it the mud, which has come all the way in, to the kitchen, and made itself at home.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:spring] The geese are back, and louder than they left.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The leaves come down faster than anyone can sweep them, so we have stopped sweeping and started calling it a carpet.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The apples came all at once this year, and now everything we eat is apple, including, I suspect, the bread.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:desert] We had rain last week, for very nearly a whole minute. People came out to look at it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:frozen] Someone here asked me what summer is like, and I had to admit I have only heard rumours.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:coast] The gulls have learned which of us carries bread. I no longer carry bread.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:swamp|home:jungle] Everything here is damp, including this letter, and probably including you by the time you finish it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:mountains] Everything here is uphill, both ways. I have checked.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:forest] A tree came down across the road, and we spent a day moving it and a week arguing about who owns the firewood.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:plains] The wind here never stops. I have weighted this letter with a stone so it does not leave before the courier.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,w:tribal] The young ones tried to answer you in paint on a hide. It came out as a picture of a muffalo, so this is the version with words.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:tribal] A boar got into the storehouse and ate more than any of us, and now the hunters are very quiet about where they were that night.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:tribal] Our storyteller has told the tale of the great hunt so often that the boar in it is now the size of a hill.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:industrial] The generator coughed all night, and so did the man who fixed it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:industrial] Our radio picks up music from somewhere far away, and nobody knows where, so we have decided it is a ghost with good taste.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:industrial] The truck broke down on the north road and has been there a week. People give directions by it now.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:spacer] Our terminal translated your letter into four languages before I could make it stop.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:spacer] The cleaning bot has started following me around. Either it is lonely or I am dirtier than I thought.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:spacer] We can cross the stars, they tell me, but nobody here can fix the door that sticks.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:herders] The herd moved twelve times this month and I moved with it. My bed is somewhere behind us on the road.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:healers] A patient tried to escape the sickhouse through the window, with his leg in a splint. We admired the effort and put him back.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:pilgrims] A pilgrim stayed with us whose boots had been mended so often there was nothing left of the boots, only the mending.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:fishers] I caught a fish this week so big that nobody believes me, and I ate the evidence.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:traders] A caravan came through selling a clock that runs backward. I bought it, so now I am always early for yesterday.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:scholars] The archive cat has slept on the same shelf for a month, and we have catalogued her under Rare.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:sextons] The bell rang itself at midnight when the rope frayed, and we are still arguing about whose turn it was to fix it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:hunters] A fox lives under the lodge now and steals one boot a week. Never a pair, always one.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:tamers] One of our young tamers tried to teach a muffalo to sit. The muffalo is still thinking it over.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:salvagers] We pulled a whole cart out of the scrap last week, wheels and all, and then found its owner asleep in it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:seers] The glass said rain, and it rained, and everyone was very impressed except me, because it always rains.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:grovekeepers] The old oak dropped a branch on the eldest root's hut. The eldest root says the oak meant it as advice.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:mercenaries] The new recruits drilled in the rain all morning and then asked if it was always like this. It is.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:artisans] An apprentice dropped a whole tray of cups, and the kiln-warden did not shout, which frightened him far more.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:linesmen] A bird built a nest on the relay, and now the whole line hums her song.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:drillers] We struck water instead of ore this week, which is good news for the well and bad news for the pay.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:citizens] We voted on the new bridge for three weeks, and then it rained and we voted to build it anyway.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:crew] The hull sprang a small leak, and the crew spent a day arguing over whose turn it was to be wet.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:editors] One of our vat-grown has decided to be a poet. The poems are all about vats.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:mechanitors] A small mech has started following the children about. Nobody told it to. We are keeping an eye on it, and it on us.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:listeners] The hum was louder this week. The first voice says it means something, and I say it means the vents want cleaning.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:vaultfolk] One of our young ones climbed the stairs and saw the sky for the first time, and came back down to tell us it is very large.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:brokers] Someone tried to pay for a shuttle seat in carrots last week. We took them. Carrots are up.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:hulking] I am told my letters are short. I am also told I break pens. These may be connected.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:refined] I had this letter copied out fair twice, because the first had a blot, and a blot is a kind of shouting.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:martial] My hand is better with a lance than a pen, so read kindly, and in order.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:underground] Someone up top told me the sun was out today. I will take their word for it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:toxic] The air here would kill most people. We find it bracing.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:fiery] Forgive the scorch at the corner. I write warm.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:cold] It has been a mild winter here, which is to say the river froze only twice as thick as usual.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:pig] My nose tells me spring is close. My nose is rarely wrong, and never quiet about it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:sea] This letter was written by the water, and may smell of it. That is not a fault.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:space] I wrote this in my bunk while the hull hummed, which is the only quiet we get up here.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:elf] I have lived long enough to see three of your colony's trees grow tall, and I still cannot tell which way the wind blows here.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:tea] We have argued about the proper way to brew tea for a week. Nobody has won. Everyone has had a great deal of tea.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:coffee] I am on my third cup as I write. That explains the speed and the handwriting.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:highlife] We had a party here last week, and I think it is still going on in the back room.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:craft] An apprentice here carved a spoon so fine nobody will let anyone eat with it.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:raider] The boys found a cart of yours on the road last month. Just kidding. Mostly.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The harvest was middling, which is the best kind, because nobody brags and nobody starves.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We have a new well at the edge of town, and the water is cold and sweet.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The road to the south is open again, and the traders are coming back.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Our roof leaks in only one place now, which is a kind of progress.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We planted a row of trees along the road. In twenty years someone will thank us, or cut them down.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We are building a bigger hall, a beam at a time, whenever there is both a beam and a time.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] We swapped seed with the next town over, and now our beans are their beans and theirs are ours, and both are doing well.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] Things are as they were at {TOWN}: busy, a little crowded, and in no particular need of anything.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] There is little to report here beyond the usual work.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,curt] We are busy here.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,curt] The road is open, if you must send anyone.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] The market was busy this month, and I came home with three things I needed and four I did not.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I have started walking out to the hill each evening to watch the light go, and I recommend it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] There is a new baby two doors down, and she already has the loudest voice in {TOWN}.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I have been teaching the little ones their letters, which is why this one is written so carefully.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] We have taken in a stray dog who has decided she is in charge of the gate.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] The young ones have been out on the hills all week, and come back brown and starving and happy.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] My knees tell me the weather before the sky does, and this week they have had a lot to say.
[theirs,everyday,a:friend,warmly] I still have the first letter you ever sent. It is in a box with the others, and the box is getting full.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] We have been mostly indoors, mending things and telling old stories.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:spring] The first green is coming up in the fields, and everyone is pretending not to be pleased.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] The days are long, and we work most of them and sit out for the rest.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The storehouse is fuller than last year, and I sleep better for it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:coast] The boats were out all week, and the catch was good.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,home:mountains] The pass is open again, and the first traders of the year came through it this week.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:tribal] The hunters brought in a muffalo last week, and we feasted for three days.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:industrial] We finally have lights along the main street, and people walk out at night just to look at them.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,w:spacer] The greenhouse dome is finished, and we have fresh tomatoes again.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:herders] The calves came early this year, and strong.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:healers] The sickhouse has been quiet this month, which is the best news a sickhouse can give.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:fishers] The river is high and brown this week, and the ferry rests while it rages.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:scholars] We had a new crate of books in from the coast, and the reading room has not been empty since.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:pious] We kept the holy days this season, all of them, and the shrine has new candles.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:nature] We let the north field go wild again this year, and the deer came back to it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:herd] The herd is fat and the grass is good, which is all a herder asks of a season.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:together] We share the work here, and the meals, and this letter too: three of us argued over every line.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:loyal] Our leader keeps well, and the town is in good order under them.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:martial] We drill at dawn and at dusk, and the walls are in good repair.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:transhuman] Two more of our people took new parts this season, and walk better for it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:tunnel] We dug a new hall under the hill this season, and it is the quietest room any of us has ever slept in.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:dark] We keep the lamps low here, as is our way. I write this by a single candle, and it is enough.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:peace] We settled a quarrel this month without a single raised hand, which is how we like it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:sea] The boats are mended and the nets are dry, and we go out again at the next tide.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:preach] You will find our faith a good one, if ever you care to hear of it. I will say no more unless asked.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:free] Every one of us here chose to be here, and any of us may leave. Few do.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:pain] We have had a hard season, and we are the better for it. That is our way.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:trade] Business has been good this season, and better than good last month.
[theirs,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,c:cannibal] We ate well this winter. You would rather not know on what, and we would rather not say.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,town:thriving|town:flourishing] {TOWN} has had a good year, and you can see it in the market.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial,town:thriving|town:flourishing] We are doing well here, better than in years, and I do not quite trust it yet.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,town:struggling|town:poor] Things are lean at {TOWN} this year, and we are counting every sack.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] Our wagons go out at the turn of the season, and there is room in them for anything {COLONY} wants to sell.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] If {COLONY} has any spare leather or good cloth, our traders would pay fairly for it.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] Our caravan passes your way before long. Have something ready to trade, and so will we.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] We have salt, iron and good rope this season, if {COLONY} is buying.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:duty] The town's accounts take most of my days, and its letters most of my evenings.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:duty] I am obliged to say that {TOWN} keeps to its agreements, and expects the same of its neighbours.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:wary] Folk here ask me what sort of people you are. I tell them I am still finding out.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:wary] We have had neighbours before who wrote kindly and came armed. I say it so you know why we are careful.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:proud] We have never needed much from our neighbours, and we are proud of it, perhaps too proud.
[theirs,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:proud] {TOWN} has stood longer than any town near it, and we have never once asked for help. I mention it only so you know us.
[theirs,everyday,a:empire,warm|cordial|cool] The court at {TOWN} is quiet this season, and the gardens are in good order.
[theirs,everyday,a:empire,warm|cordial|cool] A new knight was raised here at the last ceremony, and the hall was full to the doors.
[theirs,everyday,a:empire,warm|cordial] The musicians of the court played late into the evening, and I write this with their tunes still in my head.
[theirs,joke,a:empire,warm|cordial|cool] My stewards report a good season, which I am told is due to my wisdom, and which I suspect is due to the rain.
[theirs,joke,a:empire,warm|cordial|cool] The court has adopted a new fashion in sleeves. I am told it is magnificent. I am told this often.
[theirs,everyday,a:empire,curt|refusal] The court is occupied with weightier matters.
[theirs,everyday,a:empire,curt] My time is not my own this season.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war] These are hard days here, and I will not pretend otherwise.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war] Some nights I sit up and listen to the quiet and wonder how long it will last.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend] We have learned not to count on anything past the next harvest.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend] Look after your own. It is the only advice I have that I am sure of.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend] I keep thinking of how quickly things change, and how slowly they mend.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,town:struggling|town:poor] {TOWN} is struggling this year, and there are fewer at the table than there were.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,condolences] We buried our dead on the hill where the wind comes first in the morning. It is a good place.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,condolences] Grief takes its time here, and we are letting it.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,warning] We have doubled the watch on the walls, and nobody sleeps soundly yet.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,help] Nobody here goes hungry while another has bread. It is the only rule we have that nobody argues with.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,help] We know what an empty storehouse feels like. We have had our own.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,ransom] Whatever is decided, I hope those who are held are kept warm and fed in the meantime.
[theirs,serious,a:war] Our people and yours are at war, and I do not pretend a letter changes that. But I wanted to answer all the same.
[theirs,serious,a:war] There are graves here that your people made. I say it not to wound you, only so you know why this letter is short.
[theirs,serious,a:war] If this war ends, I hope it ends before either of us has to bury anyone else.
[theirs,serious,a:war,w:tribal] The war drums have not been quiet for a long time. I would like to hear the old songs again instead.
[theirs,serious,a:war,c:raider] We take what we need. That is our way. Do not mistake this letter for a change of heart.
[theirs,serious,a:empire] The Empire does not forget a kindness, nor a slight. I tell you so you know which this was.
[theirs,serious,a:empire] There are troubles at the edges of the Empire this season, and the court is not as merry as it was.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,w:tribal] The winter took more than it should have, and the elders say the land is testing us.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,w:industrial|w:spacer] We have people on the night watch who should be asleep, because the roads are not safe.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,c:pious] We pray for those we have lost, and for you, though you did not ask us to.
[theirs,serious,a:plain|a:friend,c:guilty] We have done things we are not proud of, and we try to make amends where we can. I say it so you know who is writing.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I have never been good at letters, so if this one wanders, follow it as best you can.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I have rewritten this letter twice, and this is the tidy version, so imagine the others.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I was told to keep this letter short. As you can see, I was told too late.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] If my handwriting defeats you, hold the page at arm's length and squint. It works for me, sometimes.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I hope this letter gets to you faster than I wrote it.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,v:blunt] I'm told letters need more than one paragraph. This is the second one.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial,v:eloquent] I could go on, and those who know me will tell you I usually do, but I will spare you.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,v:learned] I looked up how a proper letter should be written, and then wrote this one anyway.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,v:gloomy] Somebody told me to say something cheerful here. This is me trying.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,v:cheerful] I am in a good mood today, so if this letter seems too friendly, blame the soup.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,v:abrasive] I'm not one for small talk, so consider this paragraph the small talk.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:hulking] I broke two pens writing this. The third one held.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,x:refined] I have written this letter out three times to get the hand right. You are holding the third.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I find that letters say things I would never manage aloud, which may be why I like them.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] We think of the road between us more than you might guess.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial] It is good to know there are neighbours out there, even at a distance.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] We would like to know {TOWN} better, and a letter seemed the place to start.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:duty] I write on everyone's behalf here, so the words are mine but the wishes are all of ours.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,v:blunt] Not much else to say.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,v:kind] I hope everyone at {TOWN} is keeping warm and eating well.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial,v:eloquent] A letter is a slow sort of conversation, but I have come to like the pauses.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,v:learned] I have been trying to learn what I can of the lands around us, and your part of the world is the part I know least.
[ours,everyday,a:empire,warm|cordial|cool] We know little of the Empire's ways, but we mean to learn them, and to be good neighbours in the meantime.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war] These are uncertain times, and it is good to know there are people out there worth writing to.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend] Whatever comes, we would rather face it with friends.
[ours,serious,a:war] Nobody here wanted this war. I do not know if that means anything to you, but it is true.
[ours,serious,a:war] I hope one day we can write without a white flag between us.
[ours,serious,a:empire] We know the Empire has troubles of its own, and we do not ask lightly.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend,condolences] If there is anything we can do, ask, and it will be done if we can do it.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend,warning] Please take this seriously. I would rather be wrong and laughed at than right and too late.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:harvest] The harvest is in, and for once nobody is complaining about it.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:harvest] We brought the harvest in not long ago, and now everyone has opinions about what to do with it, most of them loud.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,colony:harvest,v:cheerful] The harvest is in and the storeroom smells wonderful. I have been finding excuses to walk past it.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:children] The children here are growing faster than their clothes can keep up with.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,colony:children] Our children have discovered that if they stay very quiet, nobody sends them to bed. We have discovered it too.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,colony:expecting] There will be a new face at {COLONY} before long, and we are all getting ready for it.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:newcomer] {NEWCOMER} joined us not long ago, and is still learning where everything is kept.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,colony:newcomer] {NEWCOMER} is new here and still believes everything we say, so we are being very careful.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:animals] The animals here outnumber us, and some days I think they know it.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:plenty] The stores are full, which is a good feeling, and I recommend it to everyone.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:quiet] It has been quiet here for a good while, and we are learning to enjoy it.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:quiet] It has been so quiet here lately that we have started inventing things to worry about.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:young] We are still new here, and every week something teaches us how much we do not know.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:old] We have been here long enough now that the place has its own habits, and so do we.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:traders] There are traders at our gate as I write, so the place is noisy and cheerful.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:camp] There is a camp of {CAMP} beside us for now, and they have been good neighbours.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:election] We have just chosen who speaks for us, and the arguing has mostly stopped.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial,colony:daysoon] {DAY} is coming up, and everyone is already arguing about the food.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:doctor] {DOCTOR} keeps our sick-room in good order, and the rest of us out of it if possible.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial] {COOK} has been trying new things in the kitchen, so if this letter has a stain on it, that was supper.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] {COOK} cooked for all of us last night, and I am still full as I write.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial] {ARTIST} has been at work again, and the hall is slowly filling with things that look back at you.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,colony:hungry] Food is short here this season, and we are careful with every meal.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,colony:raid] We had raiders at the gate not long ago. We held, but it cost us sleep and more.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,colony:raid:fallen] We lost people in the last fight, and we are still finding our feet.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend,colony:disaster] Things have been hard here, with {DISASTER}, and we are getting through it a day at a time.
[ours,serious,a:plain|a:friend,condition] {CONDITION} has made everything harder here, as I expect it has for you.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] Winter has come in hard here, and we spend the evenings close to the fire.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] The days are long and warm here, and we work early and rest late.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:spring] Spring is here, with all its mud and all its promise.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The leaves are turning here, and the nights have a bite to them.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] It is cold enough here that I am writing with my gloves on, which explains a good deal about the handwriting.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] It is so hot here that the ink dries before I finish the word.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:rain] It is raining as I write, so forgive the smudges.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:rain] It has rained so much here that the ducks have started looking smug.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:snow] It is snowing as I write, big quiet flakes, and everything outside has gone soft and white.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:fog] There is fog over everything today, so thick I cannot see the gate from the door.
[ours,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:storm] There is a storm overhead as I write, and every few lines the lamp shivers.
[ours,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial,weather:clear] It is a fine clear day here, the kind that makes you want to stop writing letters and go outside, so I will keep this short.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:goat] Our goat hath learned to open the gate, and we have not yet learned to stay her. I shall write again when one side prevaileth.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The miller and the baker are at feud again, and the whole village taketh sides over breakfast.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Our reeve measured the long field with a rope that proved to be two ropes. Upon parchment we are very rich in land.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The smith's apprentice set his own apron afire twice this week. He is most eager.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:bridge] The bridge washed out again, and we build it again, and it shall wash out again. Such is our sport.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:mule] I bought a mule at the fair. The mule agreeth not to the bargain, and pleadeth its case still.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,!jk:well] The well rope brake, and the bucket lieth below yet. We said a few words over it.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The road betwixt us is long, and I am told its ruts have ruts.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I counted the sheep thrice and had three answers. Either I cannot count or the sheep are plotting.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] Our steward swore the rain would hold off for the haying. The rain heard him.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] If this letter come to thee chewed at the corner, blame the rider's hound and not me.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] The snow lieth to the sills, and we are all most thoroughly acquainted with one another.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:summer] It is so hot that the hounds chase nothing, and neither do I.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:spring] Spring is come, and the mud with it, which hath come in as far as the kitchen and made itself at home.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The apples came all at once, and now all we eat is apple, the bread too, I suspect.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] My neighbour hath taken up the lute. I tell thee only that someone beyond {TOWN} may know our suffering.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] There was a wedding here, and the cake survived the dog, which no one looked for.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,!jk:goat] The goat sendeth her regards, by which I mean she ate my first draft of this letter.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:trade] Our prices are fair, our scales are true, and our ale is dreadful. Two of three is good for a town.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,m:proud] We have the best well in the shire, the oldest wall and the loudest market. I speak of it only in passing.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:healers] A patient fled the sickhouse by the window with his leg in a splint. We admired his zeal and put him back.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:mercenaries] The new recruits drilled all morning in the rain and asked if it were always thus. It is.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:artisans] An apprentice dropped a whole tray of cups, and the kiln-warden did not shout, which affrighted him far more.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:sextons] The bell rang of itself at midnight when the rope frayed, and we dispute still whose turn it was to mend it.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:hunters] A fox dwelleth under the lodge and stealeth one boot a week. Never a pair, always one.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,their:fishers] I caught a fish this week so great that none believeth me, and I ate the proof.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The harvest was middling, which is the best kind, for none boasteth and none starveth.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The new mill turneth at last, and the whole village came to see the first sack of flour come down.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] It was market day here yesterday, and I am not yet recovered.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] The road to the south is open again, and the traders come back.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] Matters stand at {TOWN} as they ever do: busy, a little crowded, and in no great need.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,curt] We are busy here.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] There is a new babe two doors hence, and she hath the loudest voice in {TOWN}.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] I walk out to the hill each evening to watch the light go, and I commend it to thee.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] We keep mostly indoors, mending things and telling old tales.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:autumn] The storehouse is fuller than last year, and I sleep the better for it.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,c:pious] We kept every holy day this season, and the chapel hath new candles.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] Our wagons go out at the turn of the season, and there is room in them for aught {COLONY} would sell.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:trade] We have salt, iron and good rope this season, if {COLONY} be buying.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:duty] The town's accounts take most of my days, and its letters most of mine evenings.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:wary] Folk here ask me what manner of people ye be. I tell them I am finding out.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain,cordial|cool,m:proud] {TOWN} hath stood longer than any town near it, and never once asked for aid. I say it only that thou mayst know us.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool,town:struggling|town:poor] Times are lean at {TOWN} this year, and we count every sack.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:friend,warmly] I keep thy first letter still, in a box with the rest, and the box groweth full.
[theirs,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,m:friend] I keep a list now of all I would tell thee, lest a letter forget aught. The list groweth long.
[theirs,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly,m:friend] I have read thy letters aloud so oft that the hound pricketh up his ears at thy name.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war] These are hard days here, and I shall not pretend otherwise.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend] Look to thine own. It is the only counsel I am sure of.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend,condolences] We laid our dead upon the hill where the wind cometh first in the morning. It is a good place.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend,warning] We have doubled the watch upon the walls, and none sleepeth soundly yet.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend,help] None goeth hungry here while another hath bread. It is the one law none disputeth.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,ransom] Whatsoever be decided, I pray those who are held be kept warm and fed meanwhile.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:war] Our folk and thine are at war, and I pretend not that a letter changeth it. Yet I would answer all the same.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:war] If this war must end, I pray it end ere either of us must bury another.
[theirs,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend,c:pious] We pray for those we have lost, and for thee, though thou didst not ask it.
[ours,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I am no great hand at letters, so if this one wander, follow it as best thou canst.
[ours,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool] I have written this letter twice over, and this is the fair copy, so imagine the others.
[ours,olde,joke,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,season:winter] It is so cold here that I write in my gloves, which explaineth much about the hand.
[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly] Letters say things I could never say aloud, which belike is why I love them.
[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,cordial|cool] We would know {TOWN} better, and a letter seemed the place to begin.
[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:harvest] The harvest is in, and for once none complaineth of it.
[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:children] Our children grow faster than their clothes can keep pace.
[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,colony:newcomer] {NEWCOMER} came to us not long since, and learneth still where all things are kept.

[ours,olde,everyday,a:plain|a:friend,warmly|cordial|cool,weather:rain] It raineth as I write, so forgive the smudges.
[ours,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war] These are uncertain times, and it is good to know there be folk worth writing to.
[ours,olde,serious,a:war] None here wished for this war. I know not if that meaneth aught to thee, but it is true.
[ours,olde,serious,a:plain|a:friend|a:war,colony:raid] Raiders came to our gate not long since. We held, but it cost us sleep and more.

[sv:machine,joke,warmly] Personal note: I have begun keeping a cat. The cat has begun keeping me.
[sv:machine,serious] Risk assessment: the region grows less safe. Precautions are advised.
[theirs,sv:hive,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] The tunnels are long now. The young are many. We hum.
[theirs,sv:hive,everyday,cordial|cool] We built. We stored. We waited for winter. It came. We are fine.
[theirs,sv:hive,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] One of us wanted a name. We discussed it. It is now called One Of Us.
[theirs,sv:hive,serious] Some of us are gone. We are fewer. We are still we.
[sv:beast,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] The rains came early, and the ground smells of new grass. The young ones roll in it.
[sv:beast,everyday,cordial|cool] There is a new scent on the east wind. Not yours. We watch it.
[sv:beast,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] Our elder caught a rabbit this week. He has told us of it every evening since.
[sv:beast,joke,warmly] One of our pups chewed the first page of this letter. This is the second page. He sends regards, and teeth marks.
[sv:beast,serious] The hunting is thin this season, and the den is quieter than it was.
[sv:green,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] The rains came, and we drank, and we grew a hand's breadth. It was a good week.
[sv:green,everyday,cordial|cool] The light is shorter now. We are slower. We do not mind.
[sv:green,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] A goat ate one of our cousins' hats. The hat was a leaf. The cousin is still upset.
[sv:green,serious] The frost came early and took some of the young shoots. We remember them in the roots.
[sv:fey,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] The mushrooms came up in a perfect ring last night, which is a fine omen, or a fine supper.
[sv:fey,everyday,cordial|cool] The dew was heavy this morning, and we counted it, as one must.
[sv:fey,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] A traveller stepped into our ring and danced for a year and a day. He says it felt like an evening. We say he dances poorly.
[sv:fey,serious] Iron came near the ring this season, and some of us are not as bright as we were.
[sv:ancient,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] I note, for your interest, that the weather here has been much as it was in my youth, which was a very long time ago.
[sv:ancient,everyday,cordial|cool] I have reorganised my library this season, by century of acquisition. It took some time.
[sv:ancient,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] A young person here asked me what life was like before. I asked them before what, and we are still discussing it.
[sv:ancient,serious] I have seen many towns rise and fall in this region. I should prefer not to see yours do so.
[sv:deep,everyday,warmly|cordial|cool] Below, the water moves. Above, the town sleeps. Between, we write.
[sv:deep,everyday,cordial|cool] The stars, wrong they were last night. Again. Note it, we did.
[sv:deep,joke,warmly|cordial|cool] A visitor asked us what we worship. Laughed, we did. Long. He left.
[sv:deep,serious] Something stirs. Not us. Watch, you should.
